name: Ayacucho Quechua

allophone_rules.notes: Vowel lowering/retraction adjacent to the uvular fricative /χ/: /a/ → [ɑ] (Wikipedia, Ayacucho Quechua).

notes: Ayacucho (Chanka) Quechua, the Southern Quechua variety of Ayacucho, Peru. Its defining difference from Cusco Quechua (quz) is the ABSENCE of the aspirated and ejective stop series — Wikipedia states plainly that Ayacucho 'lacks the aspirated and ejective series', so no ⟨ph th chh kh qh⟩ / ⟨p' t' ch' k' q'⟩ keys are asserted here; adding them would be a Cusco fact wrongly transplanted. The second difference is ⟨q⟩: Ayacucho has the uvular FRICATIVE /χ/ where Cusco has the stop /q/ (Wikipedia consonant table). Trivocalic alphabet (a, i, u); the uvular-conditioned lowering of /a i u/ to [ɑ ɛ ɔ] adjacent to /χ/ is expressed as rules, not as vowel+uvular grapheme keys. ⟨ll⟩ /ʎ/ and ⟨ñ⟩ /ɲ/ are single palatal segments. ⟨r⟩ is the trill /r/ per the Ayacucho consonant table.
